## Green Plains Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results


11/05/2026


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 180 KB](https://s201.q4cdn.com/120229500/files/doc_news/Green-Plains-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-2026.pdf)


**Results for the Third Quarter of 2026:**


- Net income attributable to Green Plains of $85.4 million, or EPS of $1.03 per diluted share
- Record adjusted EBITDA of $118.0 million, including $52.6 million from the base business and $65.4 million in 45Z production tax credit value net of discounts and other costs
- Strong operational execution, with 95% utilization across eight operating ethanol plants and record quarterly ethanol and corn oil yields supporting improved crush margins
- Cash flow from operating activities of $47.4 million through the third quarter of 2026
- Updated 2026 full-year guidance to $230 million to $250 million of adjusted EBITDA contribution from 45Z tax credit value net of discounts and other costs
- On October 29, 2026, executed agreement to monetize $250 million to $325 million of 2026 45Z production tax credits


OMAHA, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Green Plains Inc. (NASDAQ:GPRE) (“Green Plains” or the “company”) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Net income attributable to the company was $85.4 million, or $1.03 per diluted share compared to net income attributable to the company of $11.9 million or $0.17 per diluted share, for the same period in 2025. Revenues were $496.0 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared with $508.5 million for the same period last year. Core operating profitability strengthened with adjusted EBITDA of $118.0 million compared to $52.6 million for the same period in the prior year.


“Green Plains delivered record operating performance across the platform in the third quarter, demonstrating the earnings power we’ve built across the business,” said Chris Osowski, President and Chief Executive Officer of Green Plains. “Following quarter-end, the execution of our 45Z monetization agreement marked another important milestone by providing greater visibility into converting that value into cash. Together, a stronger base business and increased financial flexibility position us to invest in our platform and pursue opportunities where we believe Green Plains can create additional value for shareholders.”


“Our strong cash position and free cash flow allow us to explore a variety of options, but our standards for deploying capital have not changed,” said Ann Reis, Chief Financial Officer of Green Plains. “Every opportunity will be evaluated against risk-adjusted returns, strategic fit, and its ability to create long-term value. We intend to remain disciplined and selective as we determine where the next dollar of capital can generate attractive returns.”


**Results of Operations**


Green Plains’ ethanol production segment sold 174.9 million gallons of ethanol during the third quarter of 2026, compared with 197.3 million gallons for the same period in 2025. The consolidated ethanol crush margin was $122.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $59.6 million for the same period in 2025. The consolidated ethanol crush margin is the ethanol production segment’s operating income before depreciation and amortization, including intercompany marketing and agribusiness fees and excluding net nonethanol operating activities.


Consolidated revenues decreased $12.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the same period in 2025, primarily due to lower revenues within our ethanol production segment primarily as a result of lower volumes sold driven by the disposition of our Obion, Tennessee plant, offset by higher volumes sold and weighted average selling prices on ethanol and renewable corn oil.


Net income increased $74.6 million and adjusted EBITDA increased $65.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the same period last year primarily due to an increase of $42.3 million in Section 45Z production tax credits recorded net of discounts, other costs and selling, general and administrative expenses, higher margins in our ethanol production segment and $2.7 million lower selling, general and administrative expenses during the three months ended September 30, 2026. Interest expense decreased $39.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the same period in 2025 primarily due to prior year loan fees related to the refinancing and extinguishment of the junior mezzanine notes, partially offset by higher debt balances associated with carbon sequestration equipment. Income tax expense was $0.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with income tax expense of $0.9 million for the same period in 2025.


During the first quarter of 2026, the company elected to early adopt ASU 2025-10, *Accounting for Government Grants Received by Business Entities* . Concurrently, the company elected to change its accounting policy related to the recognition of Section 45Z production tax credits. The change in accounting policy results in the recognition of Section 45Z production tax credits by analogy under the income model of ASU 2025-10, which results in a reduction of cost of goods sold in the statements of operations and recognition as production tax credits on the consolidated balance sheets. The company previously recorded the credits under ASC 740, *Accounting for Income Taxes* , which resulted in recognition within income tax benefit in the statements of operations and deferred income taxes, net in the consolidated balance sheets. The company determined that the income model under ASU 2025-10 is preferable because it better reflects the financial benefit of Section 45Z production tax credits netted against the costs to produce the low-carbon fuels that the tax legislation was meant to incentivize. The company determined that retrospective adjustment to prior period financials is required. The impact for the change in accounting policy resulted in $26.5 million of 45Z production tax credits being recorded as a reduction of cost of goods sold during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, with related reclassifications from income tax benefit in the statements of operations. Additionally, the company has reclassified balances previously reported as deferred income taxes, net, and other long-term liabilities to production tax credits on the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2025.


**Segment Information**


The company reports the financial and operating performance for the following two operating segments: (1) ethanol production, which includes the production, storage, and transportation of ethanol, distillers grains, Ultra-High Protein, and renewable corn oil, in addition to CCS operations at our three Nebraska plants and (2) agribusiness and energy services, which includes grain handling and storage, commodity marketing and merchant trading for company-produced and third-party ethanol, distillers grains, renewable corn oil, natural gas and other commodities.

**Liquidity and Capital Resources**


As of September 30, 2026, Green Plains had $225.1 million in total cash and cash equivalents, and restricted cash, and $290.0 million available under a committed revolving credit facility, which is subject to restrictions and other lending conditions. Total debt outstanding at September 30, 2026 was $477.7 million, including $22.7 million outstanding debt under working capital revolvers and other short-term borrowing arrangements.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


Management uses EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, segment EBITDA and consolidated ethanol crush margins to measure the company’s financial performance and to internally manage its businesses. EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization excluding the change in right-of-use assets and debt issuance costs. Adjusted EBITDA includes adjustments related to restructuring costs, loss on sale of assets, impairment of assets held for sale, loss on sale of equity method investment and our proportional share of EBITDA adjustments of our equity method investees. Management believes these measures provide useful information to investors for comparison with peer and other companies. These measures should not be considered alternatives to net income or segment operating income, which are determined in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP calculations may vary from company to company. Accordingly, the company’s computation of adjusted EBITDA, segment EBITDA and consolidated ethanol crush margins may not be comparable with similarly titled measures of another company.


**About Green Plains Inc.**


Green Plains Inc. (NASDAQ: GPRE) is a leading producer of low-carbon biofuels and value-added products. The company operates a disciplined, performance-driven platform focused on maximizing yield, lowering carbon intensity, and delivering value to stakeholders. Built at scale and designed to perform across market conditions, Green Plains is focused on delivering consistent performance through operational excellence and disciplined execution. For more information, visit[www.gpreinc.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.gpreinc.com&esheet=54636301&newsitemid=20261105164186&lan=en-US&anchor=www.gpreinc.com&index=2&md5=8039ad2afa5fe96394652c49697b70ee) .
